tier_reason: Tier C stands; usability moved from copyable to reference on the enricher's code reading (not run): the resampler uses tn/delta in seconds as exponents of a per-sample pole, so the sub-sample weight is roughly constant (within 1e-4) and the output behaves as a filtered sample-and-hold, which matches the spurs visible in the repo's own HP_compare.png; the measured code is therefore not a working Holters-Parker resampler even though its operation count, and hence the timing ratios, are unaffected. process() also over-reads input[num_samples] at the 0.919 ratio and the next block re-reads it. The pinned libsamplerate 0.2.1 (aae58e2) and libsndfile 1.0.31 (949c891) builds set no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, so the documented Linux build is probably -O0 on both sides.

corrections.caveats: Likely correctness bug (code reading, not run): tn/delta in seconds is used as the exponent of a per-sample pole, so the sub-sample weight is near constant and the output acts as a filtered sample-and-hold (visible as spurs in HP_compare.png); the timing ratios are not inflated by this, but the timed code is not a working Holters-Parker resampler. process() over-reads input[num_samples] at ratio 0.919. The pinned libsamplerate and libsndfile builds set no CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE, so both sides were probably built at -O0.
